solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Villain, poor choice of poacher? (3,3)

blocks.note: an old phrase for a rotter or scoundrel
a poacher here is the kitchen pan for cooking eggs, and a rotten one is the wrong thing to put in it

annotation.surface: Someone asks whether the villain was simply a poor pick of gamekeeper's quarry.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Poacher' pulls towards a man after pheasants; it is the egg pan, and the question mark flags the pun that a bad egg is useless in it.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain idiom: calling someone a bad egg brands them untrustworthy, a mild villain.

entries.clue: Symbol to include in a witty talk (8)

indicatorNotes.to include: a word that includes something holds it inside, so the symbol wraps round the other letters

blocks.note: a badge is a symbol of membership or rank

annotation.surface: An instruction to work an emblem into a clever after-dinner speech.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In a' looks like part of the sentence's grammar, but the two little words themselves are the letters that go inside.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: badinage is light, teasing banter, borrowed from French.

entries.clue: Crack that’s hot in pierced rubbish (8)

indicatorNotes.in: 'hot in' the rest means the H is placed inside the other letters
indicatorNotes.rubbish: to rubbish something is to wreck it, so the letters of 'pierced' are wrecked into a new order

blocks.note: H = hot, as on a tap

annotation.surface: A crack in something hot that has been punctured, dismissed as rubbish.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rubbish' reads as a noun at the end, but it acts on 'pierced' as a verb; the H then sits inside the result.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to crack a code or cipher is to work out what it says.

entries.clue: Thug, don’t stop! (4)

blocks.note: a two-word urging to continue, run together

annotation.surface: Someone egging on a thug in the middle of a beating.
annotation.walkthrough: The four letters split as GO ON make the encouragement.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, the thug sense coming from American slang for a hired heavy.

entries.clue: Branch from base holds pipe down (8)

indicatorNotes.holds: something that holds another thing keeps it inside, so the base wraps round the next piece

blocks.note: of = from, as in 'a man of Kent'
the foot is the base of something
the hush sound, meaning be quiet

annotation.surface: A plumbing note: a branch pipe comes off the base and runs downwards.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pipe down' looks like plumbing, but it is the order to be quiet, and it goes inside after the first letter of the base.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a side shoot from a plant, and by extension any branch of a group.

entries.clue: Currency is with cash brought home for artist (7,5)

blocks.note: the old French, and current Swiss, unit of money
'bring home the bacon' = earn the money

annotation.surface: A painter is paid in foreign money and carries the takings home.
annotation.walkthrough: The idiom 'bring home the bacon' supplies the surname; 'with' simply attaches it to the rest.
annotation.definitionFit: By example: the Irish-born British painter (1909-92) famous for his screaming popes.

entries.clue: Tot filmed (4)

blocks.note: a tot is a small measure of spirits
past tense of what a camera crew does to a scene

annotation.surface: A small child caught on video.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tot' looks like a toddler; it is a nip of whisky.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses are plain synonyms: a small drink of spirits, and recorded on camera.

entries.clue: Piece from stentor, a tortured speaker (6)

indicatorNotes.Piece from: a piece taken from the words that follow is cut out of their run of letters

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of 'stentor' across 'a' into 'tortured'

annotation.surface: A loud-voiced figure delivers a tormented speech.
annotation.walkthrough: A stentor is a person with a very loud voice, which makes the surface sit neatly beside 'speaker'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone who makes formal public speeches.

entries.clue: Irksome busting a gut? (6)

annotation.surface: Someone finds it annoying to strain so hard.
annotation.walkthrough: One word is an adjective here and a participle there: a tiresome person, and someone having a go.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses are plain: tiresome and irritating, and making an effort.

entries.clue: Fix decay, fish on the turn (6)

indicatorNotes.on the turn: something on the turn is turning round, so the letters are reversed

annotation.surface: A fishmonger tries to deal with rot in fish that is going off.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On the turn' suggests fish going bad, which suits 'decay'; here it means turning the letters round.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of tampering: to fix the books is to falsify them.

entries.clue: Lots adopting a pig, reddish-brown (8)

indicatorNotes.adopting: the lots take in the pig, as a family takes in a child

annotation.surface: Many people adopt a pig that happens to have a reddish-brown coat.
annotation.walkthrough: The pig goes in straight after the first letter, not in the middle.
annotation.definitionFit: A colour named after the reddish-brown tropical hardwood.

entries.clue: Sweet pastry cook I suppose so snarky (8,4)

blocks.note: a tart remark is a sharp one

annotation.surface: A pastry cook gives a grudging, sarcastic verdict.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cook' looks like a noun beside 'pastry' but is the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: By example: an English almond and jam pastry named after Bakewell, a town in Derbyshire.

entries.clue: Name of person entered, by initials – forget it! (4)

indicatorNotes.initials: a name's initials are its first letters, so take the first letter of each word

blocks.note: the first letters of the four words

annotation.surface: A form-filler is told not to bother giving the entrant's name, just initials.
annotation.walkthrough: 'By' joins the wordplay to the definition at the end.
annotation.definitionFit: A casual refusal; 'forget it!' is the same flat no.

entries.clue: Striker in form at Chelsea (5)

indicatorNotes.in: the answer lies inside the words that follow

blocks.note: something struck to make a flame
the letters straddle the end of 'form', all of 'at' and the start of 'Chelsea'

annotation.surface: A football striker playing well for Chelsea.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Striker' wants to be a footballer, and Chelsea (a London football club) backs that up; it is the thing you strike to light a fire.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic sense: a match is literally the thing that is struck.

entries.clue: Accordingly, working tomorrow, perhaps? (4)

annotation.surface: Someone asks whether they will therefore be working tomorrow.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark marks 'tomorrow' as only one example of the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: tomorrow is one instance of the near future.

entries.clue: Material of sword, bargain by the sound of it? (5)

indicatorNotes.by the sound of it: judging by sound means we hear the word rather than see it

annotation.surface: A sword maker wonders if the metal was cheap.
annotation.walkthrough: The two words sound identical; the spelling comes from the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: The metal from which blades are forged; 'cold steel' is itself a word for a sword.

entries.clue: Timid type given the push by computer operator? (5)

annotation.definition2: given the push by computer operator?

blocks.clueFragment: given the push by computer operator?
blocks.note: the pointing device slid round the desk

annotation.surface: A shy worker is sacked by the computer operator.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Given the push' reads as sacked; the push is literal, across a mouse mat.
annotation.definitionFit: A metaphor: a small, quiet person is likened to the animal.

entries.clue: Feature of planet gets predator trembling (5,3,4)

indicatorNotes.trembling: something trembling is shaking, so its letters are shaken into a new order

annotation.surface: A planet's feature is so fearsome it leaves a predator shaking.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Gets' looks like a verb joining definition to wordplay, but its letters are needed in the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: By example: the giant long-lived storm on Jupiter.

entries.clue: A little woe, maths proving complex (8)

indicatorNotes.complex: something complex is intricately tangled, so the letters are tangled into a new order

annotation.surface: A student's minor grief over tricky maths homework.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Proving' links wordplay to definition, though in a maths surface it looks like a proof.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to a small degree.

entries.clue: Coin locked up in bank not long ago (8)

indicatorNotes.locked up in: something locked up in a place is shut inside it

blocks.note: to bank on is to rely on

annotation.surface: A coin was deposited in a bank vault only the other day.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bank' looks like the building for the coin; it is the verb, as in 'bank on'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: lately, a short time back.

entries.clue: Commander’s rent for shop (7,5)

blocks.note: a general is a commander; the apostrophe S is kept
rent = torn apart, past tense of rend

annotation.surface: A commanding officer's rent payment for a shop.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rent' looks like money paid to a landlord; it is the past tense of rend.
annotation.definitionFit: A kind of shop: one selling a wide range of goods, often in a village.

entries.clue: Counterbalance rotten lot (6)

blocks.note: milk that has gone off is rotten
a set = a lot, a group

annotation.surface: An attempt to balance out a batch of spoilt goods.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Counterbalance' works as noun or verb, and so does the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, as in offsetting carbon emissions.

entries.clue: Embargo on domesticated, tailless chicken (6)

indicatorNotes.on: in a down clue, a piece that is on another sits on top of it
indicatorNotes.tailless: a word without its tail has lost its last letter

annotation.surface: A ban placed on keeping a certain chicken without its tail feathers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tailless chicken' reads as one bird, but 'tailless' belongs to 'domesticated' and 'chicken' stands alone.
annotation.definitionFit: By example: a small breed of domestic fowl.

entries.clue: Highlight colours (4)

blocks.note: draw attention to, as a verb
a regiment's or ship's colours are its banner

annotation.surface: An instruction to pick out colours with a marker pen.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Colours' is a noun, as in nailing your colours to the mast.
annotation.definitionFit: Both are plain senses: to mark something for attention, and a banner.

entries.clue: Look into human family (5)

indicatorNotes.into: putting one thing into another places it inside

annotation.surface: A call to investigate the human family tree.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Look into' reads as one phrase meaning investigate; it splits into the short exclamation and the indicator.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for lineage, as in 'blood is thicker than water'.

entries.clue: Surrender when top tennis player’s announced? (4)

indicatorNotes.announced: a name that is announced is read out, so we go by how the word sounds

blocks.note: top players in a tennis draw are seeded

annotation.surface: A player gives up as soon as the top seed's name is read out.
annotation.walkthrough: In tennis the best players are ranked as seeds so they do not meet early.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to give up territory or a point.

entries.clue: Irregular at the end, polish up rough edge (4)

indicatorNotes.up: in a down clue, a word going up is read from bottom to top, so reversed
indicatorNotes.at the end: the letter at the end of the word is its last one

annotation.surface: A metalworker polishes out an irregular rough edge at the end of a piece.
annotation.walkthrough: The single letter is read first in the clue but placed last.
annotation.definitionFit: A technical sense: the ragged lip left on metal after cutting or drilling.

entries.clue: Hard wood, top of mantelpiece (4)

indicatorNotes.top of: in a down clue, the top of a word is its first letter

annotation.surface: A hardwood surface on top of the mantelpiece.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hard wood' wants to be one phrase; 'Hard' is the definition and 'wood' starts the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: solid, not yielding to pressure.

entries.clue: Fruit posed problem, being that (8)

blocks.note: a model sat, or posed, for a portrait
a sum is an arithmetic problem

annotation.surface: Some fruit set a puzzle, and that is how it was.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Posed problem' reads as one phrase, setting a puzzle; split it, and 'posed' becomes sitting for an artist.
annotation.definitionFit: By example: small easy-peel mandarin oranges; 'Fruit' can be plural.

entries.clue: Trendy comedian bashed (4,2)

blocks.note: a wit is a funny person

annotation.surface: A fashionable comedian is assaulted.
annotation.walkthrough: The two pieces overlap nothing: the H of the second simply follows the T of the first.
annotation.definitionFit: Dated slang for fashionable and up to date.

entries.clue: Cheek still turned, value in that (8)

indicatorNotes.turned: a word turned round faces the other way, so it is reversed
indicatorNotes.in: 'value in that' puts the value inside the turned word

annotation.surface: Someone still turns the other cheek and sees worth in doing so.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cheek' and 'turned' call up turning the other cheek; 'Cheek' is the definition and 'turned' acts on 'still'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: rash boldness, audacity.

entries.clue: Vulgar belly pushed back into filthy hole (6)

indicatorNotes.pushed back: something pushed back goes the other way, so the letters are reversed
indicatorNotes.into: pushing one thing into another puts it inside

blocks.note: a pigsty, or any squalid place

annotation.surface: A rude image of a belly shoved into a dirty pit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Filthy' looks like it might define the answer, but it belongs to the hole; the definition is 'Vulgar'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: dirty in the sense of indecent.
